what: First adversarial review of the four default powers (BRIEF-gui.md section 5, pull request B): five lenses (brief compliance, physics of air and form, physics of ground and recoil, code and tests, copy and layout), each finding reproduced or refuted by a skeptic with its own script. Reviewed at bf7ccc2.
script: workflow rex-gui-b-review (args {round: 1}); the script is kept in history at the end of the run

verified_ok: Build is reproducible: python3 build-data.py && node build.js on a scratch copy gives a dist/index.html and src/data.js byte-identical to the branch's.

test/powers.js --skip-off: 49/49 pass. test/calibration.js: 'all checks passed'. test/presence.js: 383 checks pass (all on a scratch copy). The powers-off fingerprint covers solo moves, plans, two-player tests, catch, walk and growth across 14,883 cases.

5a slider: #air-absorb 0–100, step 1, default 100. Read-out '100% drag-free…' and at 30% 'the air takes 70% of the drag: … still booms…'. aria-valuetext and aria-describedby are set, and the value is saved as state.airAbsorb (0–1). Cool flight's key is dropped.

5a engine: dragK multiplies the drag force in fly, flyTo and wellRun, and the heating, qDyn, shock pressure and radiation scale with it. out.air and out.ocean appear only below share 1. Their own sprint and jump flights don't use it. A thrown person's drag g is scaled by (1 − share) in the solo Throw and in the Catch.
5a: range rises with the share. The near-field blast (k × drag loss) falls to about half at 50% (t9.js). The whole-flight air energy stays nearly constant, as README decision 6 says.

5a: presets never move the slider (shots). The lower-the-slider hint shows on Throw (shots) and in the Catch: rendered, a baseball fastball at 1e9 kg with the windows and houses presets shows the hint, and at 1e6 kg it doesn't. It shows only for air presets, only at share above 0, and only when the 0% search finds an effort.

Very fast throws: the All-Star baseball at 100% has no fireball and leaves the Earth in a straight line, with the deflection stated (under 8e-8°) and the Earth, Sun and galaxy escape speeds given. With Things keep their form on it survives the fireball, and with it off at 0% it vaporizes. The Catch at 100% arrives drag-free (arriveFast) and a miss leaves the Earth. A partner toss at 100% 'escapes'.

5b: grip, launch-crush and sag give 'held together by their power'. The crush hazard is off with keepForm. Catch break-up and burn-up are blocked. Landing impacts are unchanged. The arm-wrestling table counts as held (decision 3), labelled on the page.

5c: the ground hazard is off with Unbreakable footing. Weight gives regime 'held' with text and chip. Lift shows the raw ratio with 'The ground holds: their power'. A jump past the bearing adds a push-off source. Walk prints in sand stay (fpOn equals fpOff). Sprint shows held strides.

Collide: toGround replaces the quakeHeld chip when held or partial, and Eground is no longer silently 0 for a held target. The plaster preset finds an effort with Rex bolted (shots) and with 'Jump onto him' and Rex standing (78%, rendered). The standing horizontal charge says 'never'; decision 12 is justified because the ground force is capped near μmg.

Two-player tests: all four offer the six presets. duoFacts adds ground shaking to the harm check with the powers on and says why it isn't modelled with them off (decision 13, rendered). The 'Break the ground' preset runs on real ground and the page says so.

5d: recoil is taken for the throw, punch, stomp (not the Collide stomp-launch by intent; see brief-1), pull (rope only; legs still on friction), shove and the thrower in Catch and Wrestle. The recoil-slide hazard never triggers. The recoil's toGround is counted as shaking. The bus on ice doesn't slide. The All-Star baseball doesn't move Rex. Arm wrestling, the push match and the Collide sprint are unchanged.
Saves: an old save with groundHolds/gentleHold false and coolFlight true loads with all four on and the old keys dropped (decision 15, shots).

Decision 2 is reasoned in the README and shown on the solo effort box. Decision 17 (instant growth grows up from his soles with Unbreakable footing) is stated on the page as not settled canon and in the README.

findings.title: They take their own recoil disables Collide's stomp-launch, though README and decision 4 exempt it. The page then falsely says the charger is bolted
findings.location: src/engine.js:2020 (chargeSpeed 'stomp' calls stomp(cA) without ctx.stompLaunch); src/engine.js:1383; test/powers.js:222 and :228
findings.evidence: collide() never sets ctx.stompLaunch, so with ownRecoil on, stompOnce treats the charger as bolted. Script scratchpad/reviewB1/brief/t1.js runs P.collide(rex, ollie, {source:'stomp'}) at 1e5, 1e7 and 1e9 kg. Powers off: v0 = 1.63, 20.7 and 165 m/s. With the defaults (or ownRecoil alone): noCharge 'boltedStomp' at every strength. The page (p1.js) loads {duoOpen:true, duoAction:'collide', colSrc:'stomp'} with both shown as 'Just standing' and prints: 'Bolted to the planet, Ollie’s stomp can’t launch him, so there’s nothing to land on Rex.' It then reports 'All-out: no cap needed. Nothing the lab checks in this test can do harm here'. The README says 'They take their own recoil covers his throw, punch, stomp (not Collide's stomp-launch, where the stomp is his charge)'. The test that claims this exemption ('a stomp no longer launches him (except the Collide tab's stomp-launch…)') passes stompLaunch:true by hand. The Collide check in test/powers.js runs only source:'sprint', so the real Collide path is never tested.
findings.expected: With the defaults, the stomp-launch source launches the charger as with the power off (v0 = 20.7 m/s at 1e7 kg), as decision 4 and the README state. 'Bolted to the planet' should appear only when state.anchor is bolted.
findings.fix: In chargeSpeed: `const st = stomp(Object.assign({}, cA, { stompLaunch: true }))`. In test/powers.js, add a P.collide(..., {source:'stomp'}) case with ownRecoil on that checks it equals the ownRecoil-off result.

verdict.reasoning: chargeSpeed('stomp') calls stomp(cA) without setting ctx.stompLaunch. stompOnce works out `bolted = ctx.anchor === 'bolted' || (!!ctx.ownRecoil && !ctx.stompLaunch)`, so with They take their own recoil on (a default) every Collide stomp-launch gives noCharge 'boltedStomp'. The README (line 101) and decision 4 both say Collide's stomp-launch is exempt, and the engine comment at 1381 names ctx.stompLaunch as the Collide tab's flag, but nothing in src/ ever sets it. The page then says the charger is 'Bolted to the planet' when his footing is 'Just standing', and the effort box says nothing can do harm. The test at test/powers.js:222 passes stompLaunch:true by hand. Every P.collide case in test/powers.js (lines 193, 194, 229) uses source 'sprint', so the real path is never tested. In effect a default-on power switches off a whole Collide mode and tells the reader something false.
verdict.reproduction:
verify-brief/v1.js (P.collide(rex, ollie, {source:'stomp'}), concrete, comic):
100000 off v0= 1.63 | defaults noCharge= boltedStomp | ownRecoil only noCharge= boltedStomp
10000000 off v0= 20.74 | defaults boltedStomp | ownRecoil only boltedStomp
1000000000 off v0= 165.46 | defaults boltedStomp | ownRecoil only boltedStomp
Page (verify-brief/v1p.js, localStorage {duoOpen:true,duoAction:'collide',colSrc:'stomp'}): 'Just standing' / 'Just standing' / 'Bolted to the planet, Ollie’s stomp can’t launch him, so there’s nothing to land on Rex.' / 'All-out: no cap needed. Nothing the lab checks in this test can do harm here (nearest people and buildings 5 m away), so they go all-out.'
Fix checked on a copy (v1fix.js): with the defaults, v0 = 1.63 / 20.74 / 165.46 m/s, the same as with the powers off.
verdict.better_fix: src/engine.js chargeSpeed, source 'stomp': `const st = stomp(Object.assign({}, cA, { stompLaunch: true })), f = st.bodyFlight;` (a bolted charger still gets st.bolted from ctx.anchor). Add a test to test/powers.js: `const cs = P.collide(cRr, cOr, { source: 'stomp' }), cs0 = P.collide(cR, cO, { source: 'stomp' }); ok('5d: Collide stomp-launch unchanged by own recoil', !cs.noCharge && cs.v0 === cs0.v0);`

findings.outcome: fixed: chargeSpeed passes stompLaunch (engine); test through P.collide

findings.title: Unbreakable footing on Stomp claims to take back energy that 'would have broken the ground' for any dent at all, ignoring the engine's own realBreaks
findings.location: src/engine.js:1409 (extra.absorbed = crater || hole > 0 ? E : 0) next to :1410 (realBreaks, unused); src/app.html:1601 (taken = c.unbreakable && r.absorbed > 0)
findings.evidence: The brief: footprints in soil stay; the power prevents craters, broken slabs, sinking past the bearing and punching through. The engine's own rules: hard ground breaks only at a hole of 1 cm or more, and in soil only a crater counts (realBreaks; the comment says 'a print stays'). But absorbed is E whenever the Poncelet depth is above 0 (t2.js: granite at 500 kg leaves a 2.65 µm dent, absorbed = E, realBreaks false). On the page's default Stomp view (concrete, least disruptive, 0.14% effort; p2.js) the page says: 'His stomp lands with 100 mg TNT. The ground doesn’t break: their power takes that energy back', chip 'The ground holds: their power', tile 'Energy taken back 431 J — it would have broken the ground', and 'The 100 mg TNT that would have driven his foot 0.56 mm in goes to the endless ocean'. On the same page the Hole tile reads 'barely a dent', and the ground hazard (1 cm rule) is false. On sand the 5.7 mm footprint is also 'taken back'. Hazards change too (t13.js): sand at 1e8 kg, foot at 1,115 m/s, realBreaks false. With the power on the air-blast hazard is 'never'; with it off the air hazard starts at 9.3e6 kg. So the power deletes a courtesy-ceiling hazard where by the lab's rule nothing breaks.
findings.expected: The power changes the result, and labels it, only where real ground would break (realBreaks): a crater, a hole of 1 cm or more in hard ground, or punching through. Below that, the stomp's energy goes into the ground as before, the blast stays, and the soil print stays.
findings.fix: `extra.absorbed = extra.realBreaks ? E : 0`. With unbreakable on in soil and no crater, keep holeDepth = realHole (the print). On the page, `taken = c.unbreakable && r.realBreaks`.

verdict.reasoning: stompOnce sets `extra.absorbed = rr.crater.D > 0 || rr.hole > 0 ? E : 0`. The Poncelet depth is above 0 for any foot speed, so every stomp with Unbreakable footing on counts as 'taken back'. On the next line the engine's own rule (realBreaks: a crater, or a hole of 1 cm or more in hard ground; in soil only a crater) says nothing breaks. The page keys `taken` off absorbed > 0. On the default Stomp view (concrete, least disruptive) it then says the 0.56 mm dent 'would have broken the ground', while its own Hole tile says 'barely a dent'. In sand, the footprint the brief says should stay is zeroed (holeDepth 0) and its energy is sent to the ocean. MOVES.stomp.blast subtracts absorbed, so on sand the air-blast hazard becomes 'never' over a range where by the lab's rule the ground doesn't break. The power changes results where it shouldn't act at all.
verdict.reproduction:
verify-brief/v2.js: 500 kg granite: E 1.40e3 J, realHole 2.6e-6 m, absorbed 1.40e3, realBreaks false. 500 kg concrete: realHole 1.8 mm, absorbed = E, realBreaks false. 3e4 kg sand: realHole 0.43 m (a print), absorbed = E, realBreaks false.
verify-brief/v2h2.js (sand, only unbreakable toggled): off: boom=9.34e6 kg, air=9.34e6 kg; on: boom=9.34e6 kg, air=never. At 3e7 kg: vFoot 611 m/s, hole 1.69 m, crater 0, realBreaks false, blast E 3.4e7 J off vs 0 on.
Page (v2p.js, {action:'stomp'}, defaults): 'His stomp lands with 100 mg TNT. The ground doesn’t break: their power takes that energy back…'; chip 'The ground holds: their power'; tile 'Energy taken back … it would have broken the ground: 100 mg TNT'; tile 'Hole under his foot: barely a dent'; 'The 100 mg TNT that would have driven his foot 0.56 mm in goes to the endless ocean.' On sand: '…would have driven his foot 5.7 mm in goes to the endless ocean.'
verdict.better_fix: src/engine.js stompOnce: compute rr = real() before the holdsGround branch. Set `extra.realBreaks = rr.crater.D > 0 || (!soil && rr.hole >= 0.01); extra.absorbed = extra.realBreaks ? E : 0;`. In the holdsGround branch, when `ctx.unbreakable && !ctx.groundHolds && !extra.realBreaks`, keep `holeDepth = rr.hole` (the print or dent stays, nothing is taken back). src/app.html bayStomp: `const taken = c.unbreakable && r.realBreaks;`. The legacy groundHolds path and the powers-off results are unchanged.

findings.outcome: fixed: the stomp takes back energy only where real ground breaks (realBreaks); dents and soil prints stay

findings.title: Throw tab places ground-shaking hazards 'from where it lands' (or 'from the fireball') when the shaking comes from his own push at his feet
findings.location: src/app.html:3141 (fromW), :3323 (ceiling text ce.by === 'plaster'), :3302 (only fromFire and fromPath are set; MOVES.throw.shakeFrom is never used on the solo tab)
findings.evidence: With They take their own recoil or Unbreakable footing on (the defaults), MOVES.throw.shake also counts r.toGround at his feet. The engine reports which source wins (shakeFrom), and duoFacts uses it, but the solo page doesn't. Repro (p10.js): {action:'throw', obj:'bus', angle:45, logKg:9}, 'Risk cracking the plaster' preset. The page says: 'The least effort that shakes the ground enough that plaster may crack 5 m from where it lands.' and 'Courtesy ceiling: 0.055% (lifting 551 t). Past that, the ground shakes hard enough that plaster may crack 5 m from where it lands.' For that run the engine gives shakeFrom = 'him' (t10.js), and the bus lands 92.8 m away. All-Star baseball at 100%, all-out (p3.js): 'shakes the ground enough that plaster may crack 5 m from where it lands', for a ball that 'never comes down' (the only shaking source is his feet). At 0% and 50% the same text says '5 m from the fireball'.
findings.expected: When shakeFrom(r, opt) is 'him', the shaking presets, hazards and ceiling text say '5 m from him' (or 'away'), not from where it lands or from the fireball.
findings.fix: In effortReadout, set `fromShake = move === 'throw' && M.shakeFrom(r, p.opt) === 'him'`. Make fromW take a 'shake' flag that returns ' from him' when fromShake. Use it in PRESET_WHAT.plaster and rattle and in the ceiling text for ce.by === 'plaster'.

verdict.reasoning: With They take their own recoil or Unbreakable footing on, MOVES.throw.shake also counts r.toGround at his feet, and MOVES.throw.shakeFrom says which source wins. duoFacts uses shakeFrom, but effortReadout only sets fromFire and fromPath. fromW() therefore says 'from where it lands' (or 'from the fireball') for every shaking preset, and the ceiling text for ce.by === 'plaster' hard-codes 'from where it lands' for throws. In the bus case the shaking that cracks plaster is at his feet, 92.8 m from where the bus lands. For a level All-Star ball that the same page says 'never comes down', the page still places the plaster risk 'from where it lands'. The numbers are right, but under the default powers the page's main safety readout puts the harm in the wrong place.

findings.title: Game of catch scales the fireball linearly with the share, but the Throw tab uses the snowplow at k·x. Decision 7 and the README describe the catch's model as non-linear
findings.location: src/engine.js:2745 (fireballAt: Egap = kAir * heatAt(xg)); kind, sweep, vLumpAt and mLump ignore kAir; src/app.html:2466 (catch text uses fb.sweep)
findings.evidence: Brief 5a: the game of catch gets the same treatment as the Throw tab. The README says: 'the air's share uses the game of catch's relativistic snowplow, which is not linear in the air swept: at 50% … about 74%'. t3.js, All-Star baseball, 30 m, hard throw: Catch Egap 50%/0% = 0.500 exactly. The Throw tab's fastAir gives 0.737, and the same snowplow at k·x over the 30 m gap gives 0.707. t11.js, baseball at 1e17 kg dial, D = 40 m, 50% absorbed: catch gives kind 'before' (page: 'turns into a fireball within about [full-drag sweep] of Rex’s hand, before it reaches Ollie'), Egap/E 0.277, Earr/E 0.723 'still carried toward him'. At half the drag the effective sweep doubles (D/sweep 1.35 → 0.67, so the object reaches him) and the snowplow gives 0.405. The same physics thus gets two rules on two tabs, and the catch's 'before' verdict contradicts its own Earr.
findings.expected: One rule for both tabs. Either the snowplow at k·x everywhere (heatAt(k·xg), sweep/k for kind and the text, xg·k in mLump and vLumpAt), as decision 7 and the README describe, or linear everywhere with the README corrected.
findings.fix: In fireballAt: `const xk = kAir * xg; Egap = heatAt(xk); xr = D * kAir / sweep;` use xk in mLump and vLumpAt, and report sweep / kAir for the text. Add a test that the Throw tab and the catch agree on the 50%/0% ratio for the same E and path.

verdict.reasoning: fireballAt uses `Egap = kAir * heatAt(xg)` (linear in the share). kind, sweep, rBlast, mLump and vLumpAt all ignore kAir. The Throw tab and Wrestle's throw (throwBlast → fastAir) use the snowplow at k·x, which is physically consistent: with only k of the drag acting, the object sweeps air at k times the rate. The brief asks for the same treatment in the game of catch, so one physics now has two rules. The README sentence itself is about the Throw tab, so the reviewer's 'README describes the catch as non-linear' slightly over-reads it. Because kind and sweep ignore the share, the catch's verdict and blast at 50% are word-for-word those at 0% ('turns into a fireball within about 29.7 m… before it reaches Ollie… up to 3.63 PJ'). With half the drag the effective sweep is 59.4 m, past the 37.3 m flight, so it should arrive as plasma. Correct figure: the snowplow at k·x over Dfl = 37.3 m gives Egap/E 0.389 (the reviewer's 0.405 used D = 40 m).
verdict.reproduction:
verify-brief/v4.js (catchLeg, baseball, hard, defaults):
1.81e23 kg, D 30: air 0 Egap/E 0.00197; air 0.5 Egap/E 0.000986 → catch ratio 0.500; snowplow at k·x ratio 0.707.
1e17 kg, D 40 (Dfl 37.3): air 0 kind before, sweep 29.7, Egap/E 0.555; air 0.5 kind before, sweep 29.7, Egap/E 0.277, Earr/E 0.723 → ratio 0.500 vs snowplow 0.701 (heat(kx)/E 0.389).
Page (v4p.js, {duoOpen,duoAction:'catch',cObj:'baseball',cLogD:log10(40),cStyle:'hard',logKg:17}, all-out): at 0% and at 50% the same text, 'At 62.2% of light speed the baseball turns into a fireball within about 29.7 m of Rex’s hand, before it reaches Ollie… a blast carrying up to 3.63 PJ.'
Fix checked on a copy (v4fix.js): ratio 0.707 / 0.701, kind 'plasma', sweep 59.4 m at 50%. At 0% the results are unchanged.
verdict.better_fix: src/engine.js fireballAt: `const xg = D / unit * kAir; const xr = D * kAir / sweep; const kind = …; const Egap = heatAt(xg);` (mLump and vLumpAt then use the k-scaled xg). In the 'before' branch use `Math.max(D - sweep / kAir, body.H)`, and report `sweep: sweep / kAir` in out for the page text. At kAir = 1 nothing changes (powers-off fingerprint safe). Add a test that catchLeg's Egap 50%/0% equals heatAt(0.5·x)/heatAt(x) for the same E and path.

findings.outcome: fixed: the game of catch sweeps air at the share of the rate, as the Throw tab (one rule)

findings.title: Strength ladder still lists stomp quake magnitudes with Unbreakable footing on, which the Stomp tab says it can't give

findings.expected: One rule for the same physics in both tabs. With a share k of the drag acting, the object sweeps air at k times the rate, so heat = heatAt(k*x). The half-energy length is sweep/k, and the arrives/plasma/before split uses k*D/sweep. That is what fastAir does and what decision 7 argues for.
findings.fix: In fireballAt: Egap = heatAt(kAir * xg); xr = kAir * D / sweep; vLumpAt with kAir*xg. Report sweepK = sweep/kAir and use it in bayCatch's 'half its energy' and 'before' texts and in the math line. Add a powers.js check that catch and throw agree at 50%.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced in both the engine and the page. fireballAt sets Egap = kAir * heatAt(xg), which is linear in the share. kind/xr, vLumpAt, mLump and sweep all ignore kAir. fastAir (Throw tab) uses heatAt(k*x), the snowplow at k times the sweep rate. The brief defines the share as 'the object is slowed by (1 - share) x the real drag'. With half the drag acting at every instant, the object sweeps air at half the rate, so heatAt(k x) is the consistent rule. The linear rule is only its small-heat limit, and over a long path it badly understates the loss: at 100 km and 50%, the catch lets 51% of the energy arrive, where half-rate drag leaves about 5%. So two tabs give different answers to the same physics, and decision 7's 'use the game of catch's snowplow, not linear' doesn't describe the catch. The catch's own text also contradicts its numbers. At 50% it keeps 'by about 1.96 km half its energy has turned to heat', but under its linear rule the gap heat at 50% only approaches half the energy and never reaches it; at 1.96 km it is about a quarter. The brief's letter asked for linear ('half the 0% value'), but the author rejected that for the Throw tab on physical grounds. Keeping it in the catch is an inconsistency, not a judgement call. The default (100%) and 0% (equals main) are unaffected; only intermediate shares past 1% c are wrong.

findings.evidence: Walk on loose sand: the power-on tile reads "their power holds it: 1.7× what loose sand bears". Power off: "1.7× … by the textbook rule; sand takes shallow prints instead". The engine gives an identical 8.3 mm 'print' and ratio 1.663 either way. Stomp at the default least effort: the chip says "His recoil goes into the planet: their power", but with ownRecoil off vBody is also 0 and E is identical (431.98 J; 'his weight holds him down'). Lift, car (grip 189 kPa vs 3 MPa): the chip says "Grip: object holds" while the tile says "none needed – held together by their power (Things keep their form)". Collide, Stomp-launch landing at 1.51 m/s: "The ground holds the blow: their power". Default Collide (Rex standing, 17.7 kN friction): "Unbreakable footing: the ground under Rex doesn’t break, but the push still goes in." These loads would not break concrete anyway. The brief asks that each power show 'where it changed a result'.
findings.expected: Show the label only when the result without the power differs: a real ratio above 1 and fp.held, rOwn0.vBody > 0.5, gripRatioRaw > 1, real rock rT ≥ 0.05 or a real hole.
findings.fix: Gate each label on the raw or real result the engine already returns: groundRatioRaw, rOwn0, gripRatioRaw, rock.rT, realHole.

verdict.reasoning: Four of the cited places reproduce: the power is credited although the engine result is identical without it. Brief 5 asks that each power show 'where it changed a result'. (a) Walk on sand: 'their power holds it' with an identical 8.3 mm print. footprint() returns the real print below qFail, and off, the page itself says 'sand takes shallow prints instead'. (b) The default least-effort stomp (127 kg): with ownRecoil off, E is the same 431.98 J and vBody is 0, yet the chip says 'His recoil goes into the planet: their power'. (c) Lift car: gripRatioRaw 0.063, yet the tile says 'none needed – held together by their power'. (d) Collide stomp-launch at 1.51 m/s: real ground holds too (outcome 'held' with unbreakable off), yet 'The ground holds the blow: their power'. The default Collide 'doesn’t break, but the push still goes in' item is mostly the shaking report gated by decision 13, so it is weak, not a defect. The core claim stands.
verdict.reproduction:
(a) Walk, sand: power on "108 kPa / their power holds it: 1.7× what loose sand bears", Footprint 8.3 mm. Power off: "1.7× what loose sand bears by the textbook rule; sand takes shallow prints instead", Footprint 8.3 mm.
(b) verify-copy/s/f10b.js: "kg 127.0 on: E 431.98 vBody 0 bolted true | off: E 431.98 vBody 0 footShare 1". The default Stomp page shows the chip "His recoil goes into the planet: their power".
(c) f10.js: "lift car gripRatio 0 gripRatioRaw 0.0629". The page shows the chip "Grip: object holds" and the tile "Grip plate to not crush it / none needed / held together by their power (Things keep their form)".
(d) f10c.js: stomp-launch v0 1.514, outcome held, held true, with unbreakable on and off. Page with powers off: "Rex doesn’t budge: the ground under him holds." With unbreakable on: "…the ground under him can’t give (Unbreakable footing)" plus the chip "The ground holds the blow: their power".
verdict.better_fix: Gate each label on the result without the power. Walk tile: `c.unbreakable && st.footprint.held` (else the real-ground text). Stomp chip and item: compute `const rOwn0 = c.ownRecoil && state.anchor !== 'bolted' ? P.stomp(Object.assign({}, c, { ownRecoil: false })) : null;` and show the power text only if `rOwn0 && rOwn0.vBody > 0.5`, else 'He stays put'. Lift tile: `r.gentle && r.gripRatioRaw > 1 ? 'held together by their power' : fmtArea(r.plateNeeded) …`. Collide chip and verdict: credit Unbreakable footing only when the same collide with unbreakable:false isn't 'held' (or its rock or tear check fails).

findings.outcome: fixed: Walk, Stomp recoil, Lift grip, Collide and Catch labels only where the power changed the result

findings.title: The drag energy Air resistance absorbed takes back is said to go to the endless ocean and also to stay with the object
findings.location: src/app.html:354 (slider hint), 366 (absorb hint), 1459 (Throw 'No drag' item)
findings.evidence: Slider hint: "The share of the air’s drag on what they throw that they take back (to the endless ocean, its momentum too)." Absorb hint: "(The drag that Air resistance absorbed takes back is energy the thrown thing keeps, so nothing grows from it.)" The default Throw item says "…and taken 42.5 kJ: that goes to the endless ocean. The car keeps its own energy". That counts the same 42.5 kJ in two places, though the car's energy is unchanged by the drag-free flight.
findings.expected: Bookkeeping that adds up. Either the power cancels the drag, so the car keeps the 42.5 kJ and the ocean only records the momentum and energy the air would have exchanged, or the energy goes to the ocean. Not both.
findings.fix: Use one wording everywhere, for example: 'Their power cancels the air’s drag on it (to the endless ocean, canon), so the 42.5 kJ the air would have taken stays in the car; nothing grows from it.'

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced. The slider hint and the default Throw item say the taken-back drag energy (42.5 kJ) goes to the endless ocean. The absorb hint says 'The drag that Air resistance absorbed takes back is energy the thrown thing keeps'. That gives the same energy two destinations. Canon (CLAUDE.md, Default powers) says 'The absorbed share of energy and momentum goes to the endless ocean', so the absorb hint is the line out of step. Decision 9 (no growth from it) can stand with either wording.
verdict.reproduction: Default page, Throw item: "…the air would have pushed back on it with 2.53 kN·s in all, and taken 42.5 kJ: that goes to the endless ocean. The car keeps its own energy, so nothing grows from it…". Slider hint: "…that they take back (to the endless ocean, its momentum too)." Absorb hint: "(The drag that Air resistance absorbed takes back is energy the thrown thing keeps, so nothing grows from it.)"
verdict.better_fix: Absorb hint (app.html:366): '(The drag Air resistance absorbed takes back always goes to the endless ocean, as canon says, whatever this is set to; the thrown thing simply isn’t slowed, so nothing grows from it.)'

findings.outcome: fixed: one wording (their power cancels the drag; the thing keeps the energy)

findings.title: Bolted hint says own recoil 'does the same job' as Bolted for pulls; it doesn't
findings.location: src/app.html:341
findings.evidence: Hint: "For their own throws, punches, stomps and pulls, They take their own recoil does the same job." Engine, car at a 100 t dial on concrete: P.pull with ownRecoil gives t10m 1.84 s (footLimited: 'his footing (17.7 kN) … sets the pace'). Bolted gives 0.298 s. Decision 4 and README: for a pull 'his legs still need friction'.

findings.fix: 'For their own throws, punches, stomps and shoves, They take their own recoil does the same job; for a pull it takes only the rope’s pull back (his legs still walk on friction).'

verdict.better_fix: 'For their own throws, punches, stomps and shoves, They take their own recoil does the same job; for a pull it takes only the rope’s pull back (his legs still walk on friction).'

findings.title: Straight-line text gives the Sun-escape speed without saying it is measured from the Sun
findings.location: src/app.html:1329
findings.evidence: All-Star baseball at 100%: "…the 42.1 km/s needed to leave the Sun from here, and the 445 km/s–580 km/s that published estimates give for leaving the Milky Way from the Sun’s position". The fact sun_escape_speed_at_1au displays "About 42.1 km/s, measured relative to the Sun". Its notes say a throw from the ground needs about 16.7 km/s in the best direction and about 72 km/s against Earth's motion. The arithmetic checks: √(2 × 1.3271244e20 / 1.495978707e11) = 42,122 m/s.
findings.expected: Keep the 'relative to the Sun' qualifier the research fact carries. The conclusion ('far past') still holds at 3,000 km/s and above, whatever the direction.
findings.fix: '…the 42.1 km/s needed to leave the Sun from Earth’s distance (measured from the Sun) …'.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced. The straight-line text says '42.1 km/s needed to leave the Sun from here' with no frame. The research fact's display is 'About 42.1 km/s, measured relative to the Sun', and its notes give about 16.7 km/s (best direction) to about 72 km/s for a throw from the ground. The galaxy range is likewise relative to the Galaxy, not the Sun. The arithmetic is right (sqrt(2·1.3271244e20/1.495978707e11) = 42,122 m/s) and the conclusion holds at 3,000 km/s and above. Only the qualifier the sourced fact carries is missing, which is a labelling defect under the owner's standard.
verdict.reproduction: Throw baseball, logKg 20.2587, all-out, 100% absorbed: "…it is far past the 11.2 km/s needed to escape the Earth, the 42.1 km/s needed to leave the Sun from here, and the 445 km/s–580 km/s that published estimates give for leaving the Milky Way from the Sun’s position…". research/final-environment.json sun_escape_speed_at_1au display: "About 42.1 km/s, measured relative to the Sun"; its notes: "(1) It is measured relative to the Sun, not Earth … (2) … roughly 16.7 km/s". A grep for 'relative to the Sun' in src/app.html finds nothing. python3 gives 42121.9.
verdict.better_fix: app.html:1329: '…the ' + speedOnly(es.sun) + ' needed to leave the Sun from Earth’s distance (measured relative to the Sun), and the ' + … + ' that published estimates give for leaving the Milky Way from the Sun’s position (relative to the Galaxy)…'

findings.outcome: fixed: measured from the Sun; leaves the solar system only past the Sun escape plus the Earth's orbital speed (derived from the same figures)

findings.title: New sentences put mixed or rounded-away numbers side by side
findings.location: src/app.html:1341-1342 (fastThrowText), 1481 (Throw 'Things keep their form' item)
findings.evidence: All-Star baseball, 0%, Things keep their form off: "…taking much of its energy (1.6 × 10¹² t TNT) with it. The fireball along its way takes about 280 Gt TNT (18% of it)." The parenthesis is its whole energy, not what it keeps, and the two figures are in units a reader can't compare (1.6 × 10¹² t is 1,600 Gt). Default Throw view (car at 24%): "Without it, the force on his palms would be 1× what it can take." The engine gives gripRatioRaw 1.037, which reads as 'exactly at the limit'.
findings.expected: Same unit within a sentence, and the kept share stated ('keeps about 82%, 1,300 Gt TNT'). For ratios just over 1, say 'about 4% more than it can take'.
findings.fix: In fastThrowText, give what it keeps (E − fa.E) with the same fmtTNT scale as fa.E. For ratios below 2 in this item, use a percentage ('X% more than').

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced, at the All-Star Superman strength (1.814e23 kg, logKg 23.2587), level, 0%, Things keep their form off. The fastThrowText sentence puts the whole energy (1.6 × 10¹² t TNT) in the parenthesis for 'much of its energy … with it', though it keeps about 82%. The next sentence gives the fireball as '290 Gt TNT', so the two figures sit in different units. Separately, the default Throw view rounds gripRatioRaw 1.037 to '1× what it can take'. That reads as exactly at the limit, while the item exists because the ratio is over 1. Both break CLAUDE.md's plain-numbers rule, and the second leaves the stated reason unsupported by the number shown.
verdict.reproduction: Throw baseball, logKg 23.2587, angle 0, airAbsorb 0, keepForm false, all-out: "…punches out through the atmosphere glowing, taking much of its energy (1.6 × 10¹² t TNT) with it. The fireball along its way takes about 290 Gt TNT (18% of it)." Default Throw (car, effort 24%, 22.1 t): "Without it, the force on his palms would be 1× what it can take." Engine: throwObject(ctx(22100), car, 45).gripRatioRaw = 1.0368. fmtRatio gives sig(1.0368, 2) + '×' = '1×'.
verdict.better_fix: fastThrowText: 'taking about ' + pctOfE(E - fa.E, E) + ' of its energy with it. The fireball along its way takes the rest, about ' + fmtTNT(fa.E) + '.', with both figures through one fmtTNT scale. Item at app.html:1481: `(r.gripRatioRaw < 2 ? sig(100 * (r.gripRatioRaw - 1), 2) + '% more than' : fmtRatio(r.gripRatioRaw)) + ' what it can take'`.

findings.outcome: fixed: grip below 2x as a percentage; relativistic texts rewritten
